articles.title: NostradamusGPT: The Psychology of Prophecy and How to Break Free from the Prison of Predictive Technologies
articles.highlight: 我们的悖论是：明知不确定性是宇宙的基底、创造力的熔炉、通往真理之路，却终其一生寻找确定性。
articles.summary: 这篇文章讨论人类对确定性的执念：不确定性本是宇宙的基底、创造力的熔炉和通往真理之路，我们却终生寻找确定性。作者把算法比作现代占卜的飞鸟，指出它们让人误以为能预知未来，从而回应未来并安抚焦虑。值得读它来反思预测技术如何塑造我们的心理依赖。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键提醒：算法像现代占卜的飞鸟，未必真能消除不确定性，却让人产生可预知未来的错觉。对决策者而言，应把预测结果当作有限参考，而不是安抚焦虑的确定性承诺。
articles.sourceExcerpt: This is our paradox: We know that uncertainty is the substrate of the universe, is the crucible of creativity, is the path to truth, and yet we spend our lives searching for certainty. The word auspicious derives from the Latin auspex — one who examines the flight of birds for omens and divinations of the future. Today, our birds are made of bits — wind-up larks of our own making we call algorithms — but they serve the same function: to let us believe that we can divine the future in order to respond to it; to sedate our anxieties… read article

en.highlight: We know uncertainty is the substrate of the universe, the crucible of creativity, the path to truth, yet we spend our lives searching for certainty.
en.summary: The article explores the human craving for certainty despite uncertainty being the substrate of the universe, the crucible of creativity, and the path to truth. It compares algorithms to modern birds of augury: wind-up larks made of bits that let us believe we can divine and respond to the future while sedating our anxieties. It is worth reading as a reflection on how predictive technologies shape our psychological dependence on certainty.
en.failureAnalysis: The key takeaway: predictive tools may function less as true foresight than as modern augury that soothes anxiety. For non-technical leaders, the practical constraint is to treat predictions as limited probabilities, not as certainty or emotional reassurance.
en.title: NostradamusGPT: The Psychology of Prophecy and How to Break Free from the Prison of Predictive Technologies

paperCard.method: 把“该保留哪个时间窗”建模为一个带约束的序列决策问题（马尔可夫决策过程），用强化学习智能体逐个窗口做决策：丢弃，或标记为事件的 Onset（起始）、Sustain（持续）、Offset（结束）；再用有限状态机限制每一步可选动作，保证决策顺序符合运动想象事件的生理演进。
paperCard.difference: 以前的窗口优化方法（相关性选窗 CTWS、蚁群 ACO、麻雀搜索 SSA 等）把每个候选窗口孤立地判断“好或坏”，配置离线搜索后对所有试次统一套用，容易切出碎片化、生理上不合理的窗口序列；本文让每一步决策都依赖跨窗口的历史上下文和事件阶段约束，在线逐窗自适应决策。
paperCard.innovation: 三点：一是把窗口动作空间从“保留/丢弃”改成与神经事件语义对齐的四种角色，提升可解释性；二是用有限状态机做动作掩码，把计划/执行/恢复三个阶段作为硬约束，避免出现“先 Offset 后 Onset”这类荒谬序列；三是用基于 Transformer 的历史编码器并行捕捉长距离窗口依赖，替代易梯度消失或爆炸的循环网络，训练更稳更快。
paperCard.implementation: 输入是带标签的脑电数据，按窗长 L 和步长 Δ 滑动取窗，当前窗、历史窗和试次进度组成状态；特征提取器把窗口编码成向量，判别器输出类别概率用于奖励计算；策略网络结合当前特征、历史上下文和试次进度输出动作；奖励由判别奖励（当前窗分类置信度）、时间连续奖励（窗口序列是否平滑）和终止奖励（最终分类结果）组成；强化学习用 PPO 类算法训练策略，最终把保留下来的窗口序列交给 MI 分类器分类。
paperCard.applications: 可用于需要实时响应的运动想象脑机接口，如神经康复训练、外骨骼或轮椅等辅助设备的脑控、娱乐与游戏交互、人机交互控制；其即插即用设计也可用来增强现有 EEGNet、FBCNet、ATCNet、EEGConformer 等解码器的在线表现。
technicalTerms: 运动想象（MI）：人只是想象肢体动作而不实际动，大脑感觉运动区会产生可测量的脑电变化。
脑机接口（BCI）：让大脑信号直接控制外部设备的通路。
脑电（EEG）：用头皮电极记录的大脑电活动，时间分辨率高、成本较低。
ERD/ERS：运动想象时 μ（8–13Hz）和 β（13–30Hz）节律先变弱（去同步，ERD），事件结束后又反弹增强（同步，ERS），这是判断事件阶段的生理依据。
滑动窗口：在连续信号上按固定长度不断向前平移取样，本文让算法自己决定每个窗口去留。
马尔可夫决策过程（MDP）：把序贯决策写成状态、动作、转移、奖励、折扣因子的数学框架，强化学习的标准建模方式。
有限状态机（FSM）：用一组离散状态和允许的转移规则来限制可行动作，这里用于保证决策顺序符合生理阶段。
动作掩码：在某状态下把不合法的动作直接屏蔽掉，让智能体只能选择合法动作。
Transformer 历史编码器：用自注意力机制并行建模历史窗口之间的依赖关系，比循环网络更稳定高效。
即插即用：不改动原有分类器结构，可以直接叠加到多种 MI 分类器上使用。

articles.sourceExcerpt: PREPRINT 1 Time Window Optimization for Motor Imagery Classification via Temporal Structure Embedded Reinforcement Learning Huan Luo, Na Lu, Xiaopeng Wang, and Ziyang Shang Abstract— Online motor imagery-based brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs) usually processes continuous EEG signal with fixed-length sliding windows, which is inflexible, human intervened, and misaligned with neural events. Time window optimization has shown promising improvement as a substitute solution. However, the existing optimiza- tion methods typically evaluate windows isolatedly and fail to model temporal dependencies across consecutive windows, which may produce fragmented and physiologi- cally implausible sequences.

en.highlight: TSE-RL embeds prior temporal-structure knowledge of MI events into a stable RL framework, reformulating window optimization as a constrained Markov Decision Process.
en.summary: This preprint targets the rigid, fixed-length sliding windows used in online motor imagery brain-computer interfaces, and proposes TSE-RL, a reinforcement learning framework that labels each window as Discard, Onset, Sustain or Offset under finite-state-machine constraints. It is worth reading because it improves decoding accuracy while making the learned window policy match neurophysiological principles, and it is plug-and-play with mainstream MI classifiers.
en.failureAnalysis: Only the abstract, introduction and the first half of the methods are available, so experimental details such as datasets, improvement margins and stability are unverified; all results come from simulated online experiments on public datasets rather than real online systems. The framework also relies on a prior phase division (Planning/Execution/Recovery), which may be too rigid when subjects differ in event timing.
en.title: Time Window Optimization for Motor Imagery Classification via Temporal Structure Embedded Reinforcement Learning

paperCard.problem: Online motor imagery BCIs split continuous EEG with fixed-length sliding windows whose length is set by hand; some windows cover only part of an MI event, others contain excessive pre-event baseline or artifacts, so they are misaligned with actual neural events and hurt both timeliness and accuracy.
paperCard.method: It formulates which window to keep as a constrained sequential decision problem (an MDP) and lets an RL agent decide per window: discard it, or mark it as Onset, Sustain or Offset of the event; a finite state machine restricts the legal actions so the decision order follows the physiological progression of the MI event.
paperCard.difference: Older window-optimization methods (correlation-based CTWS, ant colony optimization, sparrow search) judge each candidate window in isolation as good or bad, search configurations offline and apply them uniformly across trials, producing fragmented and physiologically implausible window sequences; this work conditions every decision on cross-window history and event-phase constraints.
paperCard.innovation: Three parts: changing the action space from retain/discard to semantic alignment with neural events; using a finite state machine for action masking so that planning/execution/recovery phases are hard constraints, preventing sequences such as Offset before Onset; and using a Transformer-based history encoder to capture long-range inter-window dependencies in parallel instead of unstable recurrent networks.
paperCard.implementation: Labeled EEG trials are cut into windows with length L and stride Δ; the state is the current window, historical windows and trial progress. A feature extractor encodes each window, a discriminator outputs class probabilities for reward computation, and a policy network combines current features, history and trial progress to choose actions. The reward combines a discrimination reward (classifier confidence), a temporal continuity reward and a termination reward (final classification outcome), and the policy is trained with RL, after which retained windows are passed to an MI classifier.
paperCard.applications: Real-time motor imagery BCIs such as neurorehabilitation training, brain-controlled assistive devices like exoskeletons or wheelchairs, entertainment and gaming interaction, and human-machine control; its plug-and-play design can also boost existing decoders such as EEGNet, FBCNet, ATCNet and EEGConformer.
technicalTerms: Motor imagery (MI): imagining a limb movement without executing it, which elicits measurable EEG changes in sensorimotor areas.
Brain-computer interface (BCI): a direct pathway letting brain signals control external devices.
EEG: scalp-recorded brain electrical activity with high temporal resolution and relatively low cost.

ERD/ERS: during motor imagery the μ (8-13 Hz) and β (13-30 Hz) rhythms desynchronize (ERD) and then rebound in synchronization (ERS) after the event, providing the physiological basis for identifying event phases.
Sliding window: repeatedly sampling fixed-length segments while moving forward along a continuous signal; here the algorithm decides whether to keep each window.
Markov Decision Process (MDP): the standard mathematical formulation of sequential decision making with states, actions, transitions, rewards and a discount factor.
Finite state machine (FSM): a set of discrete states and allowed transitions used to restrict feasible actions, here enforcing physiologically plausible orders.
Action masking: blocking illegal actions in a given state so the agent can only choose valid ones.
Transformer history encoder: a self-attention module that models dependencies among historical windows in parallel, more stable and efficient than recurrent networks.
Plug-and-play: can be stacked onto various MI classifiers without changing their architecture.

articles.title: AI is mass decompiling games. That's both awesome and scary.
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: GitHub
articles.summary: 独立游戏开发者 Popcar 谈到了近期 AI 驱动的游戏反编译浪潮：它促成了现有游戏之间各种奇怪的混搭，也带动了大量游戏保存项目，让老游戏能在新硬件甚至浏览器（借助 WebAssembly）上运行。Simon Willison 欣赏这篇文章同时呈现了正反两面——任何软件都可能被反编译，付费游戏或应用可能在违背厂商意愿的情况下被开源；但老游戏也因此更容易被移植、修改和增强。在主机厂商全面转向数字发行、服务器一关游戏就彻底玩不了的当下，这一点尤其值得关注。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键结论：反编译能力本身是中性的，同一项技术既能用于游戏保存与文化遗产抢救，也能用于商业抄袭，真正的变化是“软件难以被复制”这一长期假设开始失效。
articles.highlight: 如果 AI 能反编译游戏和软件，那么整个科技行业即将天翻地覆，任何人都能反编译别人的软件并随意使用，没人拦得住。
articles.sourceExcerpt: AI is mass decompiling games. That's both awesome and scary. Indie game developer Popcar talks about the recent wave of AI-powered decompilation of existing games, enabling weird mashups between existing games, and producing a boom in game preservation projects to get old games working on new hardware (often in a browser using WebAssembly).

en.highlight: If AI can decompile games and software, then the entire tech industry is about to explode: anybody can decompile other software and use it any way they'd like.
en.summary: Indie developer Popcar describes the recent wave of AI-powered decompilation of existing games, which enables weird mashups and a boom in preservation projects that get old games running on new hardware, often in the browser via WebAssembly. Simon Willison likes that the piece captures both sides: any software can be decompiled against its owner's wishes, yet old games can now be ported, modified and enhanced far more easily. With console makers going all in on digital and servers shutting down, this matters.
en.failureAnalysis: The key takeaway: decompilation itself is neutral, serving both preservation and outright copying; what really changes is that the long-standing assumption that software is hard to copy no longer holds.
en.title: AI Is Mass Decompiling Games. That's Both Awesome and Scary.
